Role of CryIf: Dispatcher between Crypto Service Manager and crypto drivers

The Crypto Interface (CryIf) is located in the crypto stack of the Classic Platform between the Crypto Service Manager (CSM) and one or more crypto drivers. It accepts jobs and forwards them to the configured Crypto Driver Object. This applies both to job processing via CryIf_ProcessJob [SWS_CryIf_91003] and to job cancellation, which CryIf dispatches “to the configured Crypto Driver Object” [SWS_CryIf_91014]. In the layer model of the CSM specification, CryIf is located in the ECU abstraction layer. Above it lies CSM in the service layer, below it the crypto driver in the microcontroller abstraction layer SWS CSM p. 28.

For an active job, CSM calls CryIf_ProcessJob and forwards its return value to its caller SWS CSM p. 22. CryIf itself requires the following interfaces:

  • Csm_CallbackNotification, with which “the underlying layer (CRYIF)” reports the end of a job to CSM, as well as Det_ReportRuntimeError [SWS_CryIf_91100].
  • Optionally Det_ReportError for development errors [SWS_CryIf_91101].

The API call tree of the specification distinguishes two paths: job-based services and the direct API for key management SWS CSM p. 20.

Context diagram: CryIf connects CSM queues to Crypto Driver Objects via channels, forwards feedback to CSM, and reports errors to DET. Sources: [SWS_CryIf_91003], [SWS_CryIf_91100], SWS CSM p. 28, SWS CSM p. 26

Channels, Crypto Driver Objects, and configuration

A channel is the path from a CSM queue via CryIf to a Crypto Driver Object. Each CSM queue is assigned to exactly one channel. A Crypto Driver Object represents an independent crypto “device” in hardware or software, such as an AES accelerator in an HSM or an RSA implementation in software SWS CSM p. 26.

Channels are configured in the container CryIfChannel (multiplicity 0..*, pre-compile only). It contains the parameters CryIfChannelId and CryIfDriverObjectRef. CryIfChannelId specifies which channel a CSM queue is connected to SWS CryptoInterface p. 51. Interpretation: Parameter channelId of CryIf_ProcessJob and CryIf_CancelJob is likely resolved via this container to the Crypto Driver Object referenced via CryIfDriverObjectRef [SWS_CryIf_91003] [SWS_CryIf_91014].

The content of the configuration structure CryIf_ConfigType is implementation-specific; the specification does not define it [SWS_CryIf_91118]. The include dependencies between CSM, CryIf, and the drivers Crypto_<vi>_<ai> are shown in the file structure of the specification SWS CryptoInterface p. 11.

Job processing: Operating modes and asynchronous notification

All cryptographic primitives run via the single function CryIf_ProcessJob. The field job->jobPrimitiveInputOutput.mode contains the operating modes START, UPDATE, and FINISH, which can be combined. A single call corresponds to the combination of all three modes SWS CryptoInterface p. 22. In R20-11, it depends on the configuration whether the reentrant function operates synchronously or asynchronously [SWS_CryIf_91003]. On the CSM side, an additional rule applies: If START and FINISH are set without UPDATE, CSM rejects the call with E_NOT_OK SWS CSM p. 22.

In the asynchronous case, the interfaces pass only the necessary information downward SWS CSM p. 26. The feedback then proceeds in three stages:

  1. The driver can trigger the computation via its main function. After completion, it reports the job and result to CryIf via CryIf_CallbackNotification SWS Crypto p. 27 [SWS_CryIf_91013].
  2. CryIf notifies the CSM via Csm_CallbackNotification [SWS_CryIf_91100].
  3. The CSM calls the callback configured in the job primitive SWS CSM p. 26.

This cascade is also shown in the sequence diagram of the CSM specification for R20-11 SWS CSM p. 164.

Sequence diagram: The job returns immediately; the result is passed later via callback from the driver via CryIf and CSM to the application. Sources: [SWS_CryIf_91013], [SWS_CryIf_91100], SWS CSM p. 164, SWS Crypto p. 27

The CSM cancels a running job in two ways: It removes it from its own queue or calls CryIf_CancelJob. CryIf distributes this cancellation synchronously to the Crypto Driver Object SWS CSM p. 80 [SWS_CryIf_91014]. For E_OK, the CSM calls the job's completion callback. The document passages from later releases additionally mention CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED: The cancellation then only occurs at the next suitable processing step and is reported back negatively SWS CryptoInterface p. 24. Whether R20-11 already includes this value is left open by the shortened requirement text.

Sequence diagram: The cancellation of a job is passed through to the driver via CryIf, and the result determines the feedback to the user. Sources: [SWS_CryIf_91014], SWS CSM p. 80, SWS CryptoInterface p. 46

Key references: from cryIfKeyId to the driver's key ID

CryIf uses its own key identifiers (cryIfKeyId) and translates them into the key IDs of the responsible driver. This affects the key management services CRYPTO_KEYSETVALID, CRYPTO_KEYSETINVALID, CRYPTO_RANDOMSEED, CRYPTO_KEYGENERATE, CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE, CRYPTO_KEYEXCHANGECALCPUBVAL, and CRYPTO_KEYEXCHANGECALCSECRET. For them, CryIf_ProcessJob checks whether cryIfKeyId and, if applicable, targetCryIfKeyId are within the valid range. If this is the case, CryIf sets job->cryptoKeyId and, if applicable, job->targetCryptoKeyId [SWS_CryIf_00133]. If an identifier is out of range, CryIf reports CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE to the DET and returns E_NOT_OK. For CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE, this also applies to the target identifier [SWS_CryIf_00134] [SWS_CryIf_00135] [SWS_CryIf_00141].

For key-based primitives, CryIf checks job->jobPrimitiveInfo->cryIfKeyId in the same way. These include MAC, encryption and decryption, AEAD, random number generation, as well as signature generation and verification [SWS_CryIf_00143]. In the case of job processing redirection, CryIf also translates the incoming key and key element references into the driver's values [SWS_CryIf_00136]. The document passage from later releases additionally includes CRYPTO_CUSTOM in the service list. According to the change history, this service was not added until R22-11 and therefore does not apply to R20-11 SWS CryptoInterface p. 23 SWS CryptoInterface p. 1.

Activity diagram: Depending on the service, CryIf_ProcessJob checks the key identifiers, sets the driver key IDs for key management, and aborts with E_NOT_OK in case of out-of-range errors. Sources: [SWS_CryIf_00133], [SWS_CryIf_00134], [SWS_CryIf_00135], [SWS_CryIf_00143]

Direct key management via the CryIf_Key* functions

In addition to job processing, CryIf provides a direct API for key management. A key consists of one or more key elements, such as key material, initialization vector, or seed SWS CSM p. 30. The following table summarizes the properties of the functions according to R20-11.

FunctionService IDSync/AsyncReentrancyReference
CryIf_KeyElementSet0x04synchronousnon-reentrant[SWS_CryIf_91004]
CryIf_KeySetValid0x05synchronousnon-reentrant[SWS_CryIf_91005]
CryIf_KeyElementGet0x06synchronousreentrant[SWS_CryIf_91006]
CryIf_RandomSeed0x07depending on configurationreentrant[SWS_CryIf_91007]
CryIf_KeyGenerate0x08depending on configurationreentrant[SWS_CryIf_91008]
CryIf_KeyDerive0x09synchronousreentrant[SWS_CryIf_91009]
CryIf_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal0x0asynchronousreentrant[SWS_CryIf_91010]
CryIf_KeyExchangeCalcSecret0x0bsynchronousreentrant[SWS_CryIf_91011]
CryIf_KeyElementCopy0x0fsynchronousreentrant, not for the same cryIfKeyId[SWS_CryIf_91015]
CryIf_KeyCopy0x10synchronousreentrant, not for the same cryIfKeyId[SWS_CryIf_91016]
CryIf_KeyElementCopyPartial0x12synchronousreentrant, not for the same cryIfKeyId[SWS_CryIf_91018]
CryIf_KeyGetStatus0x13synchronousnon-reentrant[SWS_CryIf_91012]
CryIf_KeySetInvalid0x14synchronousnon-reentrant[SWS_CryIf_91021]

There is an important discrepancy compared to later document passages. In R20-11, CryIf_RandomSeed and CryIf_KeyGenerate operate synchronously or asynchronously depending on configuration [SWS_CryIf_91007] [SWS_CryIf_91008]. Only starting with R21-11 are both always synchronous, as shown by the change history and the later version of key generation SWS CryptoInterface p. 1 SWS CryptoInterface p. 37. The functions for key status were newly added with R20-11 (change history: "Add functionality for key status"). For key generation, the seed must reside in element CRYPTO_KE_KEYGENERATE_SEED before generation starts SWS CSM p. 67.

Three functions control the key state [SWS_CryIf_91005] [SWS_CryIf_91021] [SWS_CryIf_91012]:

  • CryIf_KeySetValid forwards setting to valid to the driver.
  • CryIf_KeySetInvalid sets the status to invalid.
  • CryIf_KeyGetStatus returns the current state.

An invalid key results in CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID for CryIf_ProcessJob or CryIf_KeyDerive SWS CryptoInterface p. 22 SWS CryptoInterface p. 42. The CSM specification describes the usual sequence using key exchange as an example: first set the key elements, then set the key to valid SWS CSM p. 70.

State diagram: A key transitions between valid and invalid via CryIf_KeySetValid and CryIf_KeySetInvalid; operations with an invalid key fail with CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID. Sources: [SWS_CryIf_91005], [SWS_CryIf_91021], [SWS_CryIf_91012], SWS CryptoInterface p. 22

When partially copying key elements, CryIf distinguishes two cases. If the source and target keys are in the same Crypto Driver, CryIf_KeyElementCopyPartial calls the corresponding driver function and forwards its return value [SWS_CryIf_00139]. If they are in different drivers, CryIf copies them itself: It reads the element with Crypto_<vi>_<ai>_KeyElementGet, transfers the desired portion, and writes it to the target with Crypto_<vi>_<ai>_KeyElementSet [SWS_CryIf_00140]. For CryIf_KeyElementGet, resultLengthPtr has a dual role. Upon call, it contains the buffer size or, for partial access, the amount to be read. After completion, it contains the length actually stored [SWS_CryIf_91006] SWS CryptoInterface p. 30.

Activity diagram: For copies within a driver, CryIf delegates to the driver; for copies between drivers, CryIf copies itself via Get and Set. Sources: [SWS_CryIf_00139], [SWS_CryIf_00140], [SWS_CryIf_91018]

Initialization and concurrency

Prior to any other use, CryIf_Init must be called with a pointer to the selected configuration. The function is synchronous and non-reentrant [SWS_CryIf_91000]. If an API is called prior to initialization, CryIf reports CRYIF_E_UNINIT when development error detection is enabled [SWS_CryIf_00009]. The specification illustrates this, for example, for CryIf_KeyGetStatus SWS CryptoInterface p. 29. Version information is provided synchronously and reentrantly by CryIf_GetVersionInfo [SWS_CryIf_91001].

The following applies to concurrency:

  • CryIf_ProcessJob and CryIf_CancelJob are reentrant [SWS_CryIf_91003] [SWS_CryIf_91014].
  • CryIf_CallbackNotification is non-reentrant. Calls from multiple drivers must therefore not overlap [SWS_CryIf_91013].
  • The copy functions may run in parallel, but not for the same cryIfKeyId [SWS_CryIf_91015].

Behavior in the event of an error

For development errors, R20-11 defines the following codes [SWS_CryIf_00009]:

  • CRYIF_E_UNINIT (0x00): Call before initialization
  • CRYIF_E_INIT_FAILED (0x01): Initialization failed
  • CRYIF_E_PARAM_POINTER (0x02): Null pointer
  • CRYIF_E_PARAM_HANDLE (0x03): Parameter out of range
  • CRYIF_E_PARAM_VALUE (0x04): Invalid value
  • CRYIF_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH (0x05): Size of source element does not match target element

Code CRYIF_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH is likely relevant primarily when copying between drivers, because CryIf performs this copy itself [SWS_CryIf_00140].

For the range checks on keys, R20-11 uses a different designation than the error table. The requirements state CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE [SWS_CryIf_00134] [SWS_CryIf_00143], whereas the table defines CRYIF_E_PARAM_HANDLE. With R22-11, this was harmonized, and the return values after DET reports were omitted SWS CryptoInterface p. 1. For R20-11: An out-of-range error for a key identifier leads to E_NOT_OK even without development mode [SWS_CryIf_00141].

Functional errors come from the driver as crypto return values [SWS_CryIf_91020]:

  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY (0x02)
  • CRYPTO_E_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED (0x04)
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL (0x06)
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL (0x07)
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE (0x08)
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID (0x09)

CryIf forwards these values. For example, CryIf_ProcessJob can end with CRYPTO_E_BUSY, CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID, or CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH [SWS_CryIf_91003]. If setting a key element fails, its state is to be considered unknown. The application can check it with Csm_KeyGetStatus, which in turn calls CryIf_KeyGetStatus SWS CSM p. 62 SWS CSM p. 63.

CryIf_CallbackNotification also checks its inputs: Prior to initialization, it reports CRYIF_E_UNINIT, and in case of an invalid pointer CRYIF_E_PARAM_POINTER SWS CryptoInterface p. 44. For runtime errors, Det_ReportRuntimeError is provided as a required interface [SWS_CryIf_91100].

Further detailed evidence

  • [SWS_CryIf_91003] and SWS CryptoInterface p. 22: Central job interface with operating modes and return values.
  • [SWS_CryIf_00133] to [SWS_CryIf_00136], [SWS_CryIf_00141], [SWS_CryIf_00143]: Check and translation of key identifiers.
  • [SWS_CryIf_00139] and [SWS_CryIf_00140]: Partial copy within a driver and between drivers.
  • [SWS_CryIf_91013] and [SWS_CryIf_91100]: Callback chain from driver to CSM.
  • [SWS_CryIf_00009] and [SWS_CryIf_91020]: Development errors and crypto return values.
  • SWS CryptoInterface p. 51 and SWS CSM p. 26: Channel model and configuration.
  • SWS CryptoInterface p. 1: Change history for contextualizing release differences.

function CryIf_ProcessJob [SWS_CryIf_91003] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType CryIf_ProcessJob (uint32 channelId, Crypto_JobType* job);

Service CryIf_ProcessJob.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: ddb7806dc298 Provenance

The function CryIf_ProcessJob ([SWS_CryIf_91003]) forwards passed cryptographic jobs to the configured Crypto Driver Object. It accepts the channel identifier channelId as well as a pointer to the job configuration job (of type Crypto_JobType*). Depending on the configuration, the job is executed synchronously or asynchronously. The function is designed to be reentrant.

Parameter Checking and DET Reports

Prior to processing, the function performs specific checks of the key parameters:

  • If one of the services CRYPTO_KEYSETVALID, CRYPTO_KEYSETINVALID, CRYPTO_RANDOMSEED, CRYPTO_KEYGENERATE, CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE, CRYPTO_KEYEXCHANGECALCPUBVAL, or CRYPTO_KEYEXCHANGECALCSECRET is configured in job->jobPrimitiveInfo->primitiveInfo->service, job->cryIfKeyId must be within the valid range. Otherwise, CryIf_ProcessJob reports the error CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE to the DET and returns E_NOT_OK ([SWS_CryIf_00134]).
  • If the service CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE is set, the target key job->cryIfTargetKeyId must additionally be within the valid value range. In case of a range violation, the function likewise reports CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE to the DET and returns E_NOT_OK ([SWS_CryIf_00135]).

Return Values

The return value of type Std_ReturnType signals success (E_OK), general failure (E_NOT_OK), or specific error states ([SWS_CryIf_91003]):

  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The Crypto Driver Object is busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_QUEUE_FULL: The job queue is full.
  • CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED: The synchronous job was canceled.
  • Error in key state or access rights: CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID, CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH, CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL, CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL, CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE, or CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY.
  • CRYPTO_E_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED: Exhaustion of entropy pool.

This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

function CryIf_CancelJob [SWS_CryIf_91014] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType CryIf_CancelJob (uint32 channelId, Crypto_JobType* job);

This interface dispatches the job cancellation function to the configured crypto driver object.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: ac034d521f12 Provenance

use

The function CryIf_CancelJob ([SWS_CryIf_91014]) serves as the central dispatching interface of the CryIf module. Its task is to dispatch the cancellation of a crypto job to the configured crypto driver object (“dispatches the job cancellation function to the configured crypto driver object”). The interface is synchronous (Synchronous), declared in CryIf.h, and has the service ID 0x0e.

The function expects the following parameters:

  • channelId (in, uint32): Identifier of the crypto channel via which the job is routed.
  • job (inout, Crypto_JobType*): Pointer to the configuration of the crypto job, which contains structures with user- and primitive-relevant data.

Error Handling and Return Values

As a return value, the function returns a status of type Std_ReturnType:

  • E_OK: The request was successful and the job was removed.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed; the job could not be removed.
  • CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED: The specification also lists this return value. Interpretation: This value is likely passed through by the driver to indicate that the job has been canceled.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_CryIf_91014], the function is specified as reentrant (Reentrant).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

function CryIf_KeyElementSet [SWS_CryIf_91004] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType CryIf_KeyElementSet (uint32 cry If KeyId, uint32 key ElementId, const uint8* keyPtr, uint32 key Length);

This function shall dispatch the set key element function to the configured crypto driver object.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d96f62937b3e Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous function CryIf_KeyElementSet ([SWS_CryIf_91004]) forwards the request to set a key element to the configured Crypto Driver Object (dispatching). The service is provided via header CryIf.h.

The function expects the following input parameters:

  • cryIfKeyId: Unique identifier of the key whose key element is to be set.
  • keyElementId: Identifier of the specific key element to be written.
  • keyPtr: Pointer to the key data to be stored as the element value.
  • keyLength: Length of the passed key element in bytes.

Return Values and Error Handling

The function returns a status of type Std_ReturnType, which indicates the success of the operation or the cause of a failure:

  • E_OK: The request was processed successfully.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The addressed Crypto Driver Object is busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL: The operation failed because write access to the key element was denied.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE: The requested key is not available.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH: The size of the key element does not match the passed data length.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to specification [SWS_CryIf_91004], the function is classified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) and operates purely synchronously. Callers must therefore ensure that no uncoordinated concurrent calls are made to the same context or driver.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

function CryIf_KeySetValid [SWS_CryIf_91005] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType CryIf_KeySetValid (uint32 cry If KeyId);

This function shall dispatch the set key valid function to the configured crypto driver object.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: db80cb27f296 Provenance

use

The synchronous function CryIf_KeySetValid serves to set the validity of key elements by forwarding the call to the respectively configured Crypto Driver Object (Crypto Driver Object) ([SWS_CryIf_91005]). It is available via the header file CryIf.h and has the service ID 0x05 ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).

The function expects the following input parameter ([SWS_CryIf_91005]):

  • cryIfKeyId (input): Identifier of the key whose associated key elements are to be marked as valid ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).

Input/output parameters or pure output parameters are not defined for this interface ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).

Return Values and Error Handling

The function returns a status value of type Std_ReturnType as the result ([SWS_CryIf_91005]):

  • E_OK: The request was successfully executed ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the configured Crypto Driver Object is busy ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).

Concurrency and Limitations

The execution behavior of CryIf_KeySetValid is synchronous ([SWS_CryIf_91005]). With respect to reentrancy, the function is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).

Interaction

Within the CryIf architecture, CryIf_KeySetValid functions as a dispatching function that passes the setting of the key to the status "valid" to the configured driver object of the underlying driver ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).

This usage note is based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11 ([SWS_CryIf_91005]).

Usage and Semantics

The function CryIf_KeySetInvalid ([SWS_CryIf_91021]) sets the status of the key addressed via the identifier cryIfKeyId to invalid. The service is executed synchronously and is available via the header CryIf.h.

Input parameters:

  • cryIfKeyId (uint32): Identifier of the key whose status is to be invalidated.

Possible return values of type Std_ReturnType:

  • E_OK: The request was processed successfully.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is busy.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_CryIf_91021], the function is declared as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). In the event of concurrent access from multiple contexts, external synchronization by the caller is therefore likely to be required to prevent parallel executions.

Error handling

If the operation cannot be serviced immediately due to a busy driver object, the interface signals this via the status CRYPTO_E_BUSY. For general error conditions, E_NOT_OK is returned. Specific DET or DEM notifications are not indicated in the function specification.

Buffer and length management is carried out via parameters resultPtr and resultLengthPtr [SWS_CryIf_91006]:

  • Upon calling, resultLengthPtr must contain the size of the buffer provided via resultPtr [SWS_CryIf_91006].

The function returns a status of type Std_ReturnType [SWS_CryIf_91006]:

  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL: Read access was denied [SWS_CryIf_91006].

function CryIf_KeyElementCopy [SWS_CryIf_91015] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType CryIf_KeyElementCopy (uint32 cry If KeyId, uint32 key ElementId, uint32 target Cry If KeyId, uint32 target Key ElementId);

Service CryIf_KeyElementCopy.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 491e18fa517d Provenance

use

The synchronous function CryIf_KeyElementCopy ([SWS_CryIf_91015]) copies a key element from a source key to a target key. Via the input parameters cryIfKeyId and keyElementId, the source key element is specified, while targetCryIfKeyId and targetKeyElementId determine the destination of the copy operation. The service is available via the header CryIf.h.

Error Handling and Return Values

In case of success, the function returns E_OK. If the operation fails, either the general error value E_NOT_OK or one of the following specific error codes is returned ([SWS_CryIf_91015]):

  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE: The requested key element is not available.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL: Reading the source key element is not allowed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL: Writing the target key element is not permitted.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH: The sizes of the involved key elements are not compatible with each other.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The source key element is uninitialized.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_CryIf_91015], CryIf_KeyElementCopy is designed to be reentrant, but explicitly not for the same cryIfKeyId. Callers must therefore ensure that multiple threads of execution do not reference the same source key at the same time.

The synchronous function CryIf_KeyElementCopyPartial ([SWS_CryIf_91018]) serves to partially copy a key element into another key element. Based on keyElementSourceOffset, keyElementTargetOffset, and keyElementCopyLength, a specified number of bytes is transferred from the source key element (cryIfKeyId, keyElementId) to the target key element (targetCryIfKeyId, targetKeyElementId).

Regarding concurrency, the function is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same source key identifier cryIfKeyId ([SWS_CryIf_91018]). Concurrent calls for the same source key must therefore be prevented or synchronized on the caller side.

Upon successful execution, the function returns E_OK. If the operation fails, it returns E_NOT_OK or one of the following specific error codes ([SWS_CryIf_91018]):

  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The Crypto Driver Object is busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE: The requested key element is not available.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL: Reading the source key element is not allowed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL: Writing to the target key element is not allowed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH: The sizes of the involved key elements are not compatible.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The source key element is not initialized.

The caller must handle the error codes accordingly in order to catch access, length, or initialization errors as well as driver occupancies. The service is available via CryIf.h ([SWS_CryIf_91018]).

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous function CryIf_KeyCopy ([SWS_CryIf_91016]) copies all key elements of a source key (cryIfKeyId) to a target key (targetCryIfKeyId). The interface is provided via the header CryIf.h.

Error Handling and Return Values

The function reports the result via the return type Std_ReturnType with the following status and error values:

  • E_OK: The copy operation was executed successfully.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The executing Crypto Driver Object is busy.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE: The requested key element is not available.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL: Reading the source key element is not allowed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL: Writing to the target key element is not allowed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH: The sizes of the involved key elements are not compatible with each other.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The key element of the source key is not initialized.

Concurrency and Limitations

According to [SWS_CryIf_91016], the function is reentrant, but explicitly not for the same source key ID (cryIfKeyId). Interpretation: In the caller context, concurrent write access to the same target ID (targetCryIfKeyId) should probably also be avoided in order to preclude inconsistencies in the target key.

use

The synchronous interface CryIf_KeyDerive ([SWS_CryIf_91009]) forwards the key derivation request to the respectively configured Crypto Driver Object. The function is provided via the header file CryIf.h and processes two input parameters:

  • cryIfKeyId: Identifier of the source key, which serves as input for the key derivation.
  • targetCryIfKeyId: Identifier of the destination key in which the newly derived key is stored.

According to [SWS_CryIf_91009], the service is executed synchronously and is specified as reentrant.

Error Handling and Return Values

The return value of type Std_ReturnType informs the caller about the result of the dispatching or execution:

  • E_OK: The key derivation was performed successfully.
  • E_NOT_OK: The request has failed.
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY: The operation could not be executed because a required element of the source key is uninitialized.
  • CRYPTO_E_BUSY: The addressed Crypto Driver Object is in the busy state (feedback CRYPTO_E_BUSY).
  • CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID: The request fails because the state of the identified key is marked as invalid.

Concurrency and Limitations

Since CryIf_KeyDerive is designed to be reentrant ([SWS_CryIf_91009]), the function can be called concurrently from multiple contexts. Interpretation: In the event of simultaneous access to identical keys (especially regarding targetCryIfKeyId), protection against concurrency conflicts is likely required at the driver or caller level.

  <p>The function <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91003">[SWS_CryIf_91003]</a>) forwards passed cryptographic jobs to the configured Crypto Driver Object. It accepts the channel identifier <code>channelId</code> as well as a pointer to the job configuration <code>job</code> (of type <code>Crypto_JobType*</code>). Depending on the configuration, the job is executed synchronously or asynchronously. The function is designed to be reentrant.</p>
  
  <h4>Parameter Checking and DET Reports</h4>
  <p>Prior to processing, the function performs specific checks of the key parameters:</p>
  <ul>
    <li>If one of the services <code>CRYPTO_KEYSETVALID</code>, <code>CRYPTO_KEYSETINVALID</code>, <code>CRYPTO_RANDOMSEED</code>, <code>CRYPTO_KEYGENERATE</code>, <code>CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE</code>, <code>CRYPTO_KEYEXCHANGECALCPUBVAL</code>, or <code>CRYPTO_KEYEXCHANGECALCSECRET</code> is configured in <code>job-&gt;jobPrimitiveInfo-&gt;primitiveInfo-&gt;service</code>, <code>job-&gt;cryIfKeyId</code> must be within the valid range. Otherwise, <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> reports the error <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> to the DET and returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00134" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00134">[SWS_CryIf_00134]</a>).</li>
    <li>If the service <code>CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE</code> is set, the target key <code>job-&gt;cryIfTargetKeyId</code> must additionally be within the valid value range. In case of a range violation, the function likewise reports <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> to the DET and returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00135" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00135">[SWS_CryIf_00135]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> signals success (<code>E_OK</code>), general failure (<code>E_NOT_OK</code>), or specific error states (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91003">[SWS_CryIf_91003]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_QUEUE_FULL</code>: The job queue is full.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED</code>: The synchronous job was canceled.</li>
    <li>Error in key state or access rights: <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>, <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>, <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code>, <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code>, <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>, or <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED</code>: Exhaustion of entropy pool.</li>
  </ul>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="d96f62937b3e36156523d1d0366dafa54c258f4eda81a418f390dcc671815d97" data-trace-output="c64628778da6cebe29f637c5c0a49e6604a6b4cd711d3e39552479faf15b1d50" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>CryIf_KeyElementSet</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91004">[SWS_CryIf_91004]</a>) forwards the request to set a key element to the configured Crypto Driver Object (dispatching). The service is provided via header <code>CryIf.h</code>.</p>
  <p>The function expects the following input parameters:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>cryIfKeyId</code>: Unique identifier of the key whose key element is to be set.</li>
    <li><code>keyElementId</code>: Identifier of the specific key element to be written.</li>
    <li><code>keyPtr</code>: Pointer to the key data to be stored as the element value.</li>
    <li><code>keyLength</code>: Length of the passed key element in bytes.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>The function returns a status of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>, which indicates the success of the operation or the cause of a failure:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was processed successfully.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The addressed Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code>: The operation failed because write access to the key element was denied.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The requested key is not available.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The size of the key element does not match the passed data length.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>According to specification <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91004">[SWS_CryIf_91004]</a>, the function is classified as non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>) and operates purely synchronously. Callers must therefore ensure that no uncoordinated concurrent calls are made to the same context or driver.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="db80cb27f296ee33657c4baf73a61a37798c368d9c108647b0e8ed1ec0e9ac70" data-trace-output="fa20350d62befdc50ff261b9b1ca43cc3df5b4719050ace2211111de01eb382a" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous function <code>CryIf_KeySetValid</code> serves to set the validity of key elements by forwarding the call to the respectively configured Crypto Driver Object (<em>Crypto Driver Object</em>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>). It is available via the header file <code>CryIf.h</code> and has the service ID <code>0x05</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</p>
<p>The function expects the following input parameter (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>cryIfKeyId</code> (input): Identifier of the key whose associated key elements are to be marked as valid (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</li>
</ul>
<p>Input/output parameters or pure output parameters are not defined for this interface (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</p>
<h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
<p>The function returns a status value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> as the result (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successfully executed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request failed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the configured Crypto Driver Object is busy (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</li>
</ul>
<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>The execution behavior of <code>CryIf_KeySetValid</code> is synchronous (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>). With respect to reentrancy, the function is specified as non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</p>
<h4>Interaction</h4>
<p>Within the CryIf architecture, <code>CryIf_KeySetValid</code> functions as a dispatching function that passes the setting of the key to the status "valid" to the configured driver object of the underlying driver (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</p>
<p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11 (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>).</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="a8af9e5a2498adae0bbd205cd553dc636382b141767f9f3992bd8b96b76b1396" data-trace-output="1154e2df88eb7f31146ae7b5ca9318212509f685de8a73b02ebba2ae35f50537" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous function <code>CryIf_KeyElementGet</code> forwards the reading of a key element to the configured Crypto Driver Object <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>. Via the input parameters <code>cryIfKeyId</code> and <code>keyElementId</code>, the associated key as well as the desired key element are identified <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</p>
<p>Buffer and length management is carried out via parameters <code>resultPtr</code> and <code>resultLengthPtr</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>:</p>
<ul>
<li>Upon calling, <code>resultLengthPtr</code> must contain the size of the buffer provided via <code>resultPtr</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
<li>If the key element is configured for partial access, <code>resultLengthPtr</code> passes the amount of data to be read from the key element upon calling; this may differ from the buffer size <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
<li>After completion of the operation, the function writes back the amount of data actually stored in the buffer to <code>resultLengthPtr</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
<p>The function returns a status of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The query was successful <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The Crypto Driver Object is currently busy <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The requested key element is not available <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code>: Read access was denied <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The source key element is not initialized <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Concurrency and Integration</h4>
<p><code>CryIf_KeyElementGet</code> is specified as reentrant and is provided via the header file <code>CryIf.h</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a>.</p>
<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification SWS_CryIf_91006.</p>
</div>

  <p>The function <code>CryIf_RandomSeed</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91007">[SWS_CryIf_91007]</a>) forwards the random seed initialization to the configured Crypto Driver Object (dispatching). It is provided via the header file <code>CryIf.h</code> and has the service ID <code>0x07</code>.</p>
  
  <h4>Usage and Parameters</h4>
  <p>The execution semantics (synchronous or asynchronous) depend on the respective configuration. The following input parameters are passed to the function:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>cryIfKeyId</code>: Identifier of the key for which a new seed is to be generated.</li>
    <li><code>seedPtr</code>: Pointer to the memory area containing the data to feed the seed.</li>
    <li><code>seedLength</code>: Length of the seed in bytes.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>The function returns a value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successful.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The request failed because the state of the key identified via <code>cryIfKeyId</code> is "invalid".</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency</h4>
  <p>According to the specification, <code>CryIf_RandomSeed</code> is classified as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91007">[SWS_CryIf_91007]</a>).</p>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The function <code>CryIf_KeyGenerate</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91008" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91008">[SWS_CryIf_91008]</a>) forwards the key generation call to the configured Crypto Driver Object. Via the parameter <code>cryIfKeyId</code>, the identifier of the key whose value is to be updated with the newly generated key is specified. Depending on the configuration, the service operates either synchronously or asynchronously.</p>

<h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
<p>The function call returns a status of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91008" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91008">[SWS_CryIf_91008]</a>):</p>

<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: Execution could not be started because the addressed Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The request failed because a source key element is uninitialized.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The key state of the passed key is invalid (<code>invalid</code>).</li>
</ul>

<h4>Concurrency and Integration</h4>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>
    The synchronous interface <code>CryIf_KeyDerive</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91009">[SWS_CryIf_91009]</a>) forwards the key derivation request to the respectively configured Crypto Driver Object. The function is provided via the header file <code>CryIf.h</code> and processes two input parameters:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>cryIfKeyId</code>: Identifier of the source key, which serves as input for the key derivation.</li>
    <li><code>targetCryIfKeyId</code>: Identifier of the destination key in which the newly derived key is stored.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>
    According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91009">[SWS_CryIf_91009]</a>, the service is executed synchronously and is specified as reentrant.
  </p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
  <p>
    The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> informs the caller about the result of the dispatching or execution:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The key derivation was performed successfully.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The operation could not be executed because a required element of the source key is uninitialized.</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The addressed Crypto Driver Object is in the busy state (feedback <code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>).</li>
    <li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The request fails because the state of the identified key is marked as invalid.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    Since <code>CryIf_KeyDerive</code> is designed to be reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91009">[SWS_CryIf_91009]</a>), the function can be called concurrently from multiple contexts. Interpretation: In the event of simultaneous access to identical keys (especially regarding <code>targetCryIfKeyId</code>), protection against concurrency conflicts is likely required at the driver or caller level.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous function <code>CryIf_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91010">[SWS_CryIf_91010]</a>) forwards the calculation of the public value for the key exchange to the configured Crypto Driver Object. It is available via the header <code>CryIf.h</code> (service ID <code>0x0a</code>).</p>
<p>The parameter assignment is as follows:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>cryIfKeyId</code> (in): Identifier of the key to be used for the key exchange protocol.</li>
<li><code>publicValuePtr</code> (out): Pointer to the memory area in which the calculated public value is stored.</li>
<li><code>publicValueLengthPtr</code> (inout): Pointer to the length information. Upon calling, the provided buffer size of <code>publicValuePtr</code> must be passed; after completion of the service, the actual length of the generated value is stored here.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
<p>As return value, the function provides a status of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91010">[SWS_CryIf_91010]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was processed successfully.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request has failed.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: Execution failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: Execution failed because the referenced source key element is not initialized.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>: The request failed because the status of the key identified via <code>cryIfKeyId</code> is invalid.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Concurrency</h4>
<p>According to the specification, the interface is designed to be synchronous as well as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91010">[SWS_CryIf_91010]</a>).</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.</p>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The function <code>CryIf_CancelJob</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91014">[SWS_CryIf_91014]</a>) serves as the central dispatching interface of the <code>CryIf</code> module. Its task is to dispatch the cancellation of a crypto job to the configured crypto driver object (<em>“dispatches the job cancellation function to the configured crypto driver object”</em>). The interface is synchronous (<code>Synchronous</code>), declared in <code>CryIf.h</code>, and has the service ID <code>0x0e</code>.</p>
<p>The function expects the following parameters:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>channelId</code> (in, <code>uint32</code>): Identifier of the crypto channel via which the job is routed.</li>
<li><code>job</code> (inout, <code>Crypto_JobType*</code>): Pointer to the configuration of the crypto job, which contains structures with user- and primitive-relevant data.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
<p>As a return value, the function returns a status of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was successful and the job was removed.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request failed; the job could not be removed.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED</code>: The specification also lists this return value. Interpretation: This value is likely passed through by the driver to indicate that the job has been canceled.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91014">[SWS_CryIf_91014]</a>, the function is specified as reentrant (<code>Reentrant</code>).</p>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous function <code>CryIf_KeyElementCopy</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91015">[SWS_CryIf_91015]</a>) copies a key element from a source key to a target key. Via the input parameters <code>cryIfKeyId</code> and <code>keyElementId</code>, the source key element is specified, while <code>targetCryIfKeyId</code> and <code>targetKeyElementId</code> determine the destination of the copy operation. The service is available via the header <code>CryIf.h</code>.</p>

<h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
<p>In case of success, the function returns <code>E_OK</code>. If the operation fails, either the general error value <code>E_NOT_OK</code> or one of the following specific error codes is returned (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91015">[SWS_CryIf_91015]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>: The request failed because the responsible Crypto Driver Object is busy.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code>: The requested key element is not available.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code>: Reading the source key element is not allowed.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code>: Writing the target key element is not permitted.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code>: The sizes of the involved key elements are not compatible with each other.</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_EMPTY</code>: The source key element is uninitialized.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91015">[SWS_CryIf_91015]</a>, <code>CryIf_KeyElementCopy</code> is designed to be reentrant, but explicitly not for the same <code>cryIfKeyId</code>. Callers must therefore ensure that multiple threads of execution do not reference the same source key at the same time.</p>

<h4>Role of CryIf: Dispatcher between Crypto Service Manager and crypto drivers</h4>
<p>The Crypto Interface (CryIf) is located in the crypto stack of the Classic Platform between the Crypto Service Manager (CSM) and one or more crypto drivers. It accepts jobs and forwards them to the configured Crypto Driver Object. This applies both to job processing via <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91003">[SWS_CryIf_91003]</a> and to job cancellation, which CryIf dispatches “to the configured Crypto Driver Object” <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91014">[SWS_CryIf_91014]</a>. In the layer model of the CSM specification, CryIf is located in the ECU abstraction layer. Above it lies CSM in the service layer, below it the crypto driver in the microcontroller abstraction layer <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-e923d225c23cecf7.html" data-snip="FIG-e923d225c23cecf7">SWS CSM p. 28</a>.</p>
<p>For an active job, CSM calls <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> and forwards its return value to its caller <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_General_Behavior.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_General_Behavior">SWS CSM p. 22</a>. CryIf itself requires the following interfaces:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Csm_CallbackNotification</code>, with which “the underlying layer (CRYIF)” reports the end of a job to CSM, as well as <code>Det_ReportRuntimeError</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91100" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91100">[SWS_CryIf_91100]</a>.</li>
<li>Optionally <code>Det_ReportError</code> for development errors <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91101" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91101">[SWS_CryIf_91101]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>The API call tree of the specification distinguishes two paths: job-based services and the direct API for key management <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-adc263ea09fdd9be.html" data-snip="FIG-adc263ea09fdd9be">SWS CSM p. 20</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Context diagram: CryIf connects CSM queues to Crypto Driver Objects via channels, forwards feedback to CSM, and reports errors to DET. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91003">[SWS_CryIf_91003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91100" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91100">[SWS_CryIf_91100]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-e923d225c23cecf7.html" data-snip="FIG-e923d225c23cecf7">SWS CSM p. 28</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_2_2_2_Queuing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_2_2_2_Queuing">SWS CSM p. 26</a></p>

<h4>Channels, Crypto Driver Objects, and configuration</h4>
<p>A channel is the path from a CSM queue via CryIf to a Crypto Driver Object. Each CSM queue is assigned to exactly one channel. A Crypto Driver Object represents an independent crypto “device” in hardware or software, such as an AES accelerator in an HSM or an RSA implementation in software <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_2_2_2_Queuing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_2_2_2_Queuing">SWS CSM p. 26</a>.</p>
<p>Channels are configured in the container <code>CryIfChannel</code> (multiplicity 0..*, pre-compile only). It contains the parameters <code>CryIfChannelId</code> and <code>CryIfDriverObjectRef</code>. <code>CryIfChannelId</code> specifies which channel a CSM queue is connected to <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_10_2_4_CryIfChannel.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_10_2_4_CryIfChannel">SWS CryptoInterface p. 51</a>. Interpretation: Parameter <code>channelId</code> of <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> and <code>CryIf_CancelJob</code> is likely resolved via this container to the Crypto Driver Object referenced via <code>CryIfDriverObjectRef</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91003">[SWS_CryIf_91003]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91014">[SWS_CryIf_91014]</a>.</p>
<p>The content of the configuration structure <code>CryIf_ConfigType</code> is implementation-specific; the specification does not define it <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91118" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91118">[SWS_CryIf_91118]</a>. The include dependencies between CSM, CryIf, and the drivers <code>Crypto_&lt;vi&gt;_&lt;ai&gt;</code> are shown in the file structure of the specification <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-48a8d7cf6718b640.html" data-snip="FIG-48a8d7cf6718b640">SWS CryptoInterface p. 11</a>.</p>

<h4>Job processing: Operating modes and asynchronous notification</h4>
<p>All cryptographic primitives run via the single function <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code>. The field <code>job-&gt;jobPrimitiveInputOutput.mode</code> contains the operating modes START, UPDATE, and FINISH, which can be combined. A single call corresponds to the combination of all three modes <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface">SWS CryptoInterface p. 22</a>. In R20-11, it depends on the configuration whether the reentrant function operates synchronously or asynchronously <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91003">[SWS_CryIf_91003]</a>. On the CSM side, an additional rule applies: If START and FINISH are set without UPDATE, CSM rejects the call with <code>E_NOT_OK</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_1_Normal_Operation.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_1_Normal_Operation">SWS CSM p. 22</a>.</p>
<p>In the asynchronous case, the interfaces pass only the necessary information downward <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_1_3_Asynchronous_Job_Processing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_1_3_Asynchronous_Job_Processing">SWS CSM p. 26</a>. The feedback then proceeds in three stages:</p>
<ol>
<li>The driver can trigger the computation via its main function. After completion, it reports the job and result to CryIf via <code>CryIf_CallbackNotification</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing">SWS Crypto p. 27</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91013">[SWS_CryIf_91013]</a>.</li>
<li>CryIf notifies the CSM via <code>Csm_CallbackNotification</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91100" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91100">[SWS_CryIf_91100]</a>.</li>
<li>The CSM calls the callback configured in the job primitive <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_1_3_Asynchronous_Job_Processing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_1_3_Asynchronous_Job_Processing">SWS CSM p. 26</a>.</li>
</ol>
<p>This cascade is also shown in the sequence diagram of the CSM specification for R20-11 <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-5c6a4eece7e55c6b.html" data-snip="FIG-5c6a4eece7e55c6b">SWS CSM p. 164</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Sequence diagram: The job returns immediately; the result is passed later via callback from the driver via CryIf and CSM to the application. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91013">[SWS_CryIf_91013]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91100" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91100">[SWS_CryIf_91100]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-5c6a4eece7e55c6b.html" data-snip="FIG-5c6a4eece7e55c6b">SWS CSM p. 164</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_7_2_2_2_Asynchronous_Job_Processing">SWS Crypto p. 27</a></p>
<p>The CSM cancels a running job in two ways: It removes it from its own queue or calls <code>CryIf_CancelJob</code>. CryIf distributes this cancellation synchronously to the Crypto Driver Object <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CSM_SECTION_8_3_11_Job_Cancellation_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CSM_SECTION_8_3_11_Job_Cancellation_Interface">SWS CSM p. 80</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91014">[SWS_CryIf_91014]</a>. For <code>E_OK</code>, the CSM calls the job's completion callback. The document passages from later releases additionally mention <code>CRYPTO_E_JOB_CANCELED</code>: The cancellation then only occurs at the next suitable processing step and is reported back negatively <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_3_Job_Cancellation_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_3_Job_Cancellation_Interface">SWS CryptoInterface p. 24</a>. Whether R20-11 already includes this value is left open by the shortened requirement text.</p>

Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91014">[SWS_CryIf_91014]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CSM_SECTION_8_3_11_Job_Cancellation_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CSM_SECTION_8_3_11_Job_Cancellation_Interface">SWS CSM p. 80</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_5_2_Optional_interfaces.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYPTO_SECTION_8_5_2_Optional_interfaces">SWS CryptoInterface p. 46</a></p>

<h4>Key references: from cryIfKeyId to the driver's key ID</h4>
<p>CryIf uses its own key identifiers (<code>cryIfKeyId</code>) and translates them into the key IDs of the responsible driver. This affects the key management services <code>CRYPTO_KEYSETVALID</code>, <code>CRYPTO_KEYSETINVALID</code>, <code>CRYPTO_RANDOMSEED</code>, <code>CRYPTO_KEYGENERATE</code>, <code>CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE</code>, <code>CRYPTO_KEYEXCHANGECALCPUBVAL</code>, and <code>CRYPTO_KEYEXCHANGECALCSECRET</code>. For them, <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> checks whether <code>cryIfKeyId</code> and, if applicable, <code>targetCryIfKeyId</code> are within the valid range. If this is the case, CryIf sets <code>job-&gt;cryptoKeyId</code> and, if applicable, <code>job-&gt;targetCryptoKeyId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00133">[SWS_CryIf_00133]</a>. If an identifier is out of range, CryIf reports <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> to the DET and returns <code>E_NOT_OK</code>. For <code>CRYPTO_KEYDERIVE</code>, this also applies to the target identifier <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00134" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00134">[SWS_CryIf_00134]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00135" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00135">[SWS_CryIf_00135]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00141" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00141">[SWS_CryIf_00141]</a>.</p>
<p>For key-based primitives, CryIf checks <code>job-&gt;jobPrimitiveInfo-&gt;cryIfKeyId</code> in the same way. These include MAC, encryption and decryption, AEAD, random number generation, as well as signature generation and verification <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00143">[SWS_CryIf_00143]</a>. In the case of job processing redirection, CryIf also translates the incoming key and key element references into the driver's values <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00136" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00136">[SWS_CryIf_00136]</a>. The document passage from later releases additionally includes <code>CRYPTO_CUSTOM</code> in the service list. According to the change history, this service was not added until R22-11 and therefore does not apply to R20-11 <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_1_Dispatch_Key_IDs.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_1_Dispatch_Key_IDs">SWS CryptoInterface p. 23</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_General_Overview.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_General_Overview">SWS CryptoInterface p. 1</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Activity diagram: Depending on the service, CryIf_ProcessJob checks the key identifiers, sets the driver key IDs for key management, and aborts with E_NOT_OK in case of out-of-range errors. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00133">[SWS_CryIf_00133]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00134" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00134">[SWS_CryIf_00134]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00135" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00135">[SWS_CryIf_00135]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00143">[SWS_CryIf_00143]</a></p>

<h4>Direct key management via the CryIf_Key* functions</h4>
<p>In addition to job processing, CryIf provides a direct API for key management. A key consists of one or more key elements, such as key material, initialization vector, or seed <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_2_3_Key_Management.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_7_2_2_3_Key_Management">SWS CSM p. 30</a>. The following table summarizes the properties of the functions according to R20-11.</p>
<table>
<thead><tr><th>Function</th><th>Service ID</th><th>Sync/Async</th><th>Reentrancy</th><th>Reference</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyElementSet</code></td><td>0x04</td><td>synchronous</td><td>non-reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91004">[SWS_CryIf_91004]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeySetValid</code></td><td>0x05</td><td>synchronous</td><td>non-reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyElementGet</code></td><td>0x06</td><td>synchronous</td><td>reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_RandomSeed</code></td><td>0x07</td><td>depending on configuration</td><td>reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91007">[SWS_CryIf_91007]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyGenerate</code></td><td>0x08</td><td>depending on configuration</td><td>reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91008" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91008">[SWS_CryIf_91008]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyDerive</code></td><td>0x09</td><td>synchronous</td><td>reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91009">[SWS_CryIf_91009]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyExchangeCalcPubVal</code></td><td>0x0a</td><td>synchronous</td><td>reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91010">[SWS_CryIf_91010]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyExchangeCalcSecret</code></td><td>0x0b</td><td>synchronous</td><td>reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91011" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91011">[SWS_CryIf_91011]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyElementCopy</code></td><td>0x0f</td><td>synchronous</td><td>reentrant, not for the same <code>cryIfKeyId</code></td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91015">[SWS_CryIf_91015]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyCopy</code></td><td>0x10</td><td>synchronous</td><td>reentrant, not for the same <code>cryIfKeyId</code></td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91016" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91016">[SWS_CryIf_91016]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyElementCopyPartial</code></td><td>0x12</td><td>synchronous</td><td>reentrant, not for the same <code>cryIfKeyId</code></td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91018">[SWS_CryIf_91018]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeyGetStatus</code></td><td>0x13</td><td>synchronous</td><td>non-reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91012">[SWS_CryIf_91012]</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>CryIf_KeySetInvalid</code></td><td>0x14</td><td>synchronous</td><td>non-reentrant</td><td><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91021">[SWS_CryIf_91021]</a></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>There is an important discrepancy compared to later document passages. In R20-11, <code>CryIf_RandomSeed</code> and <code>CryIf_KeyGenerate</code> operate synchronously or asynchronously depending on configuration <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91007">[SWS_CryIf_91007]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91008" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91008">[SWS_CryIf_91008]</a>. Only starting with R21-11 are both always synchronous, as shown by the change history and the later version of key generation <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_General_Overview.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_General_Overview">SWS CryptoInterface p. 1</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_4_5_Key_Generation_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_4_5_Key_Generation_Interface">SWS CryptoInterface p. 37</a>. The functions for key status were newly added with R20-11 (change history: "Add functionality for key status"). For key generation, the seed must reside in element <code>CRYPTO_KE_KEYGENERATE_SEED</code> before generation starts <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CSM_SECTION_8_3_8_5_Key_Generation_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CSM_SECTION_8_3_8_5_Key_Generation_Interface">SWS CSM p. 67</a>.</p>
<p>Three functions control the key state <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91021">[SWS_CryIf_91021]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91012">[SWS_CryIf_91012]</a>:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>CryIf_KeySetValid</code> forwards setting to valid to the driver.</li>
<li><code>CryIf_KeySetInvalid</code> sets the status to invalid.</li>
<li><code>CryIf_KeyGetStatus</code> returns the current state.</li>
</ul>
<p>An invalid key results in <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code> for <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> or <code>CryIf_KeyDerive</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface">SWS CryptoInterface p. 22</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_4_6_Key_Derivation_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_4_6_Key_Derivation_Interface">SWS CryptoInterface p. 42</a>. The CSM specification describes the usual sequence using key exchange as an example: first set the key elements, then set the key to valid <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_8_7_Key_Exchange_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_8_7_Key_Exchange_Interface">SWS CSM p. 70</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">State diagram: A key transitions between valid and invalid via CryIf_KeySetValid and CryIf_KeySetInvalid; operations with an invalid key fail with CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91005">[SWS_CryIf_91005]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91021">[SWS_CryIf_91021]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91012">[SWS_CryIf_91012]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_2_Job_Processing_Interface">SWS CryptoInterface p. 22</a></p>
<p>When partially copying key elements, CryIf distinguishes two cases. If the source and target keys are in the same Crypto Driver, <code>CryIf_KeyElementCopyPartial</code> calls the corresponding driver function and forwards its return value <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00139" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00139">[SWS_CryIf_00139]</a>. If they are in different drivers, CryIf copies them itself: It reads the element with <code>Crypto_&lt;vi&gt;_&lt;ai&gt;_KeyElementGet</code>, transfers the desired portion, and writes it to the target with <code>Crypto_&lt;vi&gt;_&lt;ai&gt;_KeyElementSet</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00140" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00140">[SWS_CryIf_00140]</a>. For <code>CryIf_KeyElementGet</code>, <code>resultLengthPtr</code> has a dual role. Upon call, it contains the buffer size or, for partial access, the amount to be read. After completion, it contains the length actually stored <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91006" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91006">[SWS_CryIf_91006]</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_4_3_Key_Extraction_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_4_3_Key_Extraction_Interface">SWS CryptoInterface p. 30</a>.</p>
