<p class="diagram-note">Activity diagram: For copies within a driver, CryIf delegates to the driver; for copies between drivers, CryIf copies itself via Get and Set. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00139" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00139">[SWS_CryIf_00139]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00140" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00140">[SWS_CryIf_00140]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91018">[SWS_CryIf_91018]</a></p>

<h4>Initialization and concurrency</h4>
<p>Prior to any other use, <code>CryIf_Init</code> must be called with a pointer to the selected configuration. The function is synchronous and non-reentrant <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91000" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91000">[SWS_CryIf_91000]</a>. If an API is called prior to initialization, CryIf reports <code>CRYIF_E_UNINIT</code> when development error detection is enabled <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00009">[SWS_CryIf_00009]</a>. The specification illustrates this, for example, for <code>CryIf_KeyGetStatus</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_4_2_Key_Status_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_4_2_Key_Status_Interface">SWS CryptoInterface p. 29</a>. Version information is provided synchronously and reentrantly by <code>CryIf_GetVersionInfo</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91001">[SWS_CryIf_91001]</a>.</p>
<p>The following applies to concurrency:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> and <code>CryIf_CancelJob</code> are reentrant <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91003">[SWS_CryIf_91003]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91014">[SWS_CryIf_91014]</a>.</li>
<li><code>CryIf_CallbackNotification</code> is non-reentrant. Calls from multiple drivers must therefore not overlap <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91013">[SWS_CryIf_91013]</a>.</li>
<li>The copy functions may run in parallel, but not for the same <code>cryIfKeyId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91015">[SWS_CryIf_91015]</a>.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Behavior in the event of an error</h4>
<p>For development errors, R20-11 defines the following codes <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00009">[SWS_CryIf_00009]</a>:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>CRYIF_E_UNINIT</code> (0x00): Call before initialization</li>
<li><code>CRYIF_E_INIT_FAILED</code> (0x01): Initialization failed</li>
<li><code>CRYIF_E_PARAM_POINTER</code> (0x02): Null pointer</li>
<li><code>CRYIF_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> (0x03): Parameter out of range</li>
<li><code>CRYIF_E_PARAM_VALUE</code> (0x04): Invalid value</li>
<li><code>CRYIF_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code> (0x05): Size of source element does not match target element</li>
</ul>
<p>Code <code>CRYIF_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code> is likely relevant primarily when copying between drivers, because CryIf performs this copy itself <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00140" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00140">[SWS_CryIf_00140]</a>.</p>
<p>For the range checks on keys, R20-11 uses a different designation than the error table. The requirements state <code>CRYPTO_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00134" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00134">[SWS_CryIf_00134]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00143">[SWS_CryIf_00143]</a>, whereas the table defines <code>CRYIF_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code>. With R22-11, this was harmonized, and the return values after DET reports were omitted <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_General_Overview.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_General_Overview">SWS CryptoInterface p. 1</a>. For R20-11: An out-of-range error for a key identifier leads to <code>E_NOT_OK</code> even without development mode <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00141" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00141">[SWS_CryIf_00141]</a>.</p>
<p>Functional errors come from the driver as crypto return values <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91020">[SWS_CryIf_91020]</a>:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code> (0x02)</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED</code> (0x04)</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_READ_FAIL</code> (0x06)</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_WRITE_FAIL</code> (0x07)</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE</code> (0x08)</li>
<li><code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code> (0x09)</li>
</ul>
<p>CryIf forwards these values. For example, <code>CryIf_ProcessJob</code> can end with <code>CRYPTO_E_BUSY</code>, <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_NOT_VALID</code>, or <code>CRYPTO_E_KEY_SIZE_MISMATCH</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91003">[SWS_CryIf_91003]</a>. If setting a key element fails, its state is to be considered unknown. The application can check it with <code>Csm_KeyGetStatus</code>, which in turn calls <code>CryIf_KeyGetStatus</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_8_1_Key_Setting_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_3_8_1_Key_Setting_Interface">SWS CSM p. 62</a> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CSM_SECTION_8_3_8_2_Key_Status_Interface.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CSM_SECTION_8_3_8_2_Key_Status_Interface">SWS CSM p. 63</a>.</p>
<p><code>CryIf_CallbackNotification</code> also checks its inputs: Prior to initialization, it reports <code>CRYIF_E_UNINIT</code>, and in case of an invalid pointer <code>CRYIF_E_PARAM_POINTER</code> <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_4_Callback_notifications.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_CRYIF_SECTION_8_4_Callback_notifications">SWS CryptoInterface p. 44</a>. For runtime errors, <code>Det_ReportRuntimeError</code> is provided as a required interface <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91100" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91100">[SWS_CryIf_91100]</a>.</p>

<li><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00133">[SWS_CryIf_00133]</a> to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00136" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00136">[SWS_CryIf_00136]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00141" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00141">[SWS_CryIf_00141]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_00143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_00143">[SWS_CryIf_00143]</a>: Check and translation of key identifiers.</li>

<li><a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91013">[SWS_CryIf_91013]</a> and <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CryIf_91100" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CryIf_91100">[SWS_CryIf_91100]</a>: Callback chain from driver to CSM.</li>
